suggestions: Tamper evidence command: the phase-auto skill says to work only inside the repo, so copy into a git-ignored folder in the repo (for example `rm -rf data/cache/kd_tamper && cp -R exports/<dir> data/cache/kd_tamper`) instead of /tmp. The `rm -rf` also stops `cp -R` nesting the copy on a re-run. Pass `--ledger data/cache/memory_demo.duckdb` too. Without it, verify-evidence checks against data/memory.duckdb, which has none of the demo rows, so the ledger check also FAILs and the evidence no longer shows that the one edited file alone caused the failure.
Reseed with os.replace: close and checkpoint the temp DuckDB file before replacing. Also remove any stale `<memory>.wal` and `<tmp>.wal`, so DuckDB never replays an old WAL onto the new file.

Copying a ledger (the demo scratch copy and the ledger_copy fixture): copy only after the source connection is closed and checkpointed, or copy through DuckDB with ATTACH and COPY FROM DATABASE. The head-equality check would catch a bad copy, but it is cheaper to prevent one.

Append-only scan: limit each pattern to one statement before the build, for example `\bUPDATE\s+ledger\b` or `DROP\s+TABLE\s+(IF\s+EXISTS\s+)?ledger\b`. Otherwise `store/duck.py:261` (`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS {name}`) plus a later mention of 'ledger' could cause a false positive, and narrowing the regex mid-build could look like weakening a test. Consider adding `ALTER TABLE ledger`.

Fix the `valid_at(rows, case_id, t_valid)` signature in step 4: the text says it uses the rows known at `known_at`, so add an explicit `known_at` parameter. test_valid_time_differs_from_transaction_time needs it.

A3 says proposals about existing members are never pending, yet the three-links test approves a proposal for DELTA, which is already the founder, and expects three members_added with new_member=false on one. State in A6 that decide_link accepts any active, undecided proposal for the case, whether or not it is pending, so phase 7's UI and this test agree.
The rule-9 negative test uses 'John Smith'. Use an obviously made-up token instead (for example 'Person Name Example'), to stay clear of rule 1's 'no real names'.

D-096: planted cases come from `scenario.p1_flights[*].assessment`, which ties the memory package to the P1 list in config. Note that only the base-side assessment fields are used (label, author, assessed time), never P1 membership as a label. Or key the seeding off the assessment id.
D-099: state explicitly that rule 4 governs the generated data, and that no data or content hash depends on the CSPRNG key apart from pubkey.pem and manifest.sig.
In EXIT_CHECK.md, record the exact number of tests `-k memory` collects, and the fast-test arithmetic (497 − 3 + N), so the gate's no-drop check is easy to audit.
